title: Ten 0.1s added in a loop don't equal 1 - but since Python 3.12, sum() gives exactly 1.0 and the loop still doesn't
assumption: Accumulating ten $0.10 charges one at a time gives exactly $1.00, and Python's sum() is just a loop in disguise.

input.display: a loop adding 0.1 ten times, vs. sum([0.1] * 10)
input.description: A running total built up line-by-line as items are scanned or charges applied, e.g. ten $0.10 surcharges added to an order as it is built.

what_goes_wrong: A hand-written accumulator (`total += 0.1` ten times) ends at 0.9999999999999999, not 1.0, in both Python and JavaScript - but on Python 3.12 and later the built-in `sum([0.1]*10)` prints exactly 1.0 (on 3.11 and earlier it printed 0.9999999999999999, same as the loop), so swapping a loop for `sum()`, or upgrading Python, silently changes the answer.
why: Each addition rounds to the nearest representable double, and those small rounding errors compound across ten sequential additions, landing one ULP below 1.0. In Python 3.12, CPython's built-in `sum()` switched to compensated (Neumaier) summation for floats: it carries the rounding error of each addition in a separate correction term and adds it back at the end, so for this input it no longer reproduces the naive loop's error. It is not the same as `math.fsum` (which is exactly rounded for every input); the docs only promise "higher accuracy and better commutativity on most builds". JavaScript has no built-in equivalent in Node 22 - `reduce` and a hand-rolled loop behave identically because both are plain sequential addition.

repros.code:
total = 0.0
for _ in range(10):
    total += 0.1
print(total, total == 1.0)
print(sum([0.1] * 10), sum([0.1] * 10) == 1.0)

fix: Do the running total in integer minor units (cents) or with a Decimal type, not floating-point dollars. Don't rely on `sum()` happening to be more accurate than a loop in a particular Python version - that's an implementation detail, not a guarantee for every float computation.

sources.title: Python docs: 15.1. Floating-Point Arithmetic: Issues and Limitations

test_cases.note: A totaling function should not assume their_function(ten dimes) == 1.0 unless it works in integer cents or Decimal; don't trust that it happens to round correctly on today's runtime.
